explanation:
## How Dollar-Cost Averaging Bitcoin Works

You invest the **same dollar amount every month** regardless of price. When BTC is cheap you automatically buy more coins; when it's expensive you buy fewer. Over a full cycle this pulls your **blended average cost below the simple average of the prices you paid** — the core mathematical advantage of DCA in a volatile asset.

The math:

```
BTC accumulated = Σ (monthly contribution ÷ BTC price that month)
Total invested  = monthly contribution × number of months
Current value   = BTC accumulated × current price
ROI             = (Current value − Total invested) ÷ Total invested
```

The calculator uses a single **average entry price** as a shortcut for the month-by-month sum. Pick that number from the realistic range your timeframe actually spanned — the table below helps.

## Why DCA Suits Bitcoin Specifically

- **Volatility is the point**: BTC routinely swings ±50% in a year. DCA turns that volatility into an advantage by mechanically buying more during crashes.
- **No timing required**: starting a DCA at the 2021 top still recovered by 2024 — the schedule absorbed the drawdown a lump sum would have suffered in full.
- **Behavioral discipline**: automating the buy removes the temptation to stop during a 2018- or 2022-style winter, which is exactly when accumulation pays off most.
- **Cycle awareness**: Bitcoin has historically moved in ~4-year halving cycles. A DCA that spans a full cycle is far less sensitive to your start date than one of a few months.

## Common Mistakes

- **Stopping during crashes** — this discards the cheapest coins and defeats the strategy.
- **Over-allocating** — BTC is speculative; size the contribution to what you can hold through an 80% drawdown.
- **Ignoring fees** — recurring small buys on high-fee exchanges can quietly erode returns; prefer low-fee recurring-buy products.
- **Treating past returns as a forecast** — Bitcoin's history is short and extraordinary; it does not guarantee future results.

This is an educational estimate, not investment advice. Crypto is high-risk; never invest more than you can afford to lose.

faq.a: DCA means investing a fixed amount regularly, regardless of price, to reduce timing risk and smooth out market volatility.

faq.q: Why is DCA better than lump sum investing?
faq.a: DCA reduces the impact of market timing. In rising markets, lump sum wins. In volatile markets, DCA often performs better with less emotional stress.

faq.q: How often should I execute DCA trades?
faq.a: Monthly is most common and manageable. Weekly reduces volatility further but requires more discipline. Daily is overkill for most investors.

faq.q: Can I automate Bitcoin DCA investments?
faq.a: Yes. Many crypto exchanges and investment apps offer automated DCA programs so your investments happen without manual intervention.

faq.q: What does historical Bitcoin DCA performance show?
faq.a: Historical data demonstrates that consistent Bitcoin investing from various starting points would have generated significant returns, but past performance doesn't guarantee future results.

faq.q: How are taxes calculated on DCA profits?
faq.a: Each sale triggers a taxable event. Track your cost basis carefully and consult a tax advisor for capital gains reporting requirements.

faq.q: Should I modify my DCA when Bitcoin prices spike?
faq.a: No. Discipline is essential. Stopping or reducing DCA during price peaks defeats the strategy's purpose. Stay committed to your plan.

faq.q: What returns should I expect from Bitcoin DCA?
faq.a: Bitcoin is volatile and speculative. Historical returns don't predict future performance. Never invest more than you can afford to lose.
